position: STAY on Next.js/TypeScript and pay down the confirmed debt with a scoped, shippable refactor. Do not rewrite in Go or Java.
summary: Start with the premise: the app already IS React 19 and Tailwind v4, and every theme is already nothing but a validated set of CSS custom properties (themes/contract.ts:23-40, app/globals.css:1 '@import tailwindcss' with 104 custom properties). 'Port to React and Tailwind so we can do richer themes' is not a port — it is the stack in the repository today, and the richer-themes work is a form and a token set, not a language. What a Go or Java rebuild would actually replace is the 19,332 server-side lines under app/ and lib/ plus middleware.ts; the 15,921 lines under components/, modules/ and themes/ (55% of source) are React and Tailwind either way and get carried over or thrown away for nothing. Second: 49 code-review findings survived adversarial verification with real=true, 26 of them mattering inside twelve months. I read all 49 against the code. Two are high severity and they are the same root cause: the Supabase driver — the one production runs on — is executed by zero behavioural tests and drifted from the memory driver, so unpublished photographs reached guests (lib/db/repository.ts:343 declares liveOnly; lib/db/supabase-repository.ts ignored it; lib/db/memory-repository.ts:924 honours it). Of the 49, I can attribute exactly one, in part, to TypeScript (structural typing let an implementation drop an options parameter) and two to Next.js App Router specifics (cookies() defeating ISR; `next lint`'s default directory set). The other 46 are SQL shape, cron scheduling, missing staging, a 10-second heartbeat, stale documentation and untested UI — all of which a Go rewrite reproduces on day one and calls a fresh start. Third, the empirical answer to 'unmanageable': that highest-severity finding was located, half-fixed and pinned with a new regression test in the working tree within a day of being found (lib/db/supabase-repository.ts:1632-1641 and the untracked tests/unit/supabase-query-shape.test.ts, both uncommitted as of 16 Sept). A codebase where the worst bug in it is found and fixed in a day by one person and an agent is not unmanageable; it is under-instrumented. The refactor is 3.5 engineer-months, delivered in slices that each ship, and the first slice ships the same week. The rewrite is 9-14 engineer-months before the first wedding streams, against 6 orgs, 5 catalogues and pre-revenue.
architecture: Keep every seam the codebase already has; fix what runs behind them. (1) The persistence seam — lib/db/repository.ts is 404 lines and 103 methods with two implementations, and CLAUDE.md argues for it explicitly. It is correct and it is the thing that is under-tested, not mis-designed. The refactor adds a driver-conformance suite: one table of behavioural assertions executed against MemoryRepository and against a real Supabase branch in CI, so the two drivers cannot silently disagree again. Alongside it, `supabase gen types typescript` produces a generated Database type that makes the ~20 hand-written field-to-column maps (lib/db/supabase-repository.ts:87, :107, and ~18 more) compile-checked against the real schema. That closes, at the compiler, the exact class of safety the Go argument is asking for — and it is available today, unused. (2) The authorisation seam — lib/catalogue-access.ts is 88 lines and holds the whole guest access rule in one readable ordering: lapsed before published, premiere before passcode, draft is never a 404 (:37-62). That file is the product's trust model and it should not be retyped in another language for sport. lib/admin/session.ts is the equivalent for org scoping and it currently holds perfectly across 34 admin route files and 11 admin pages; the refactor pins it with a test that walks the route tree for the five real guard names (requireOperator, requireOwnedCatalogue, requireEditableCatalogue, getOperatorSession, getSessionOrg) against an allowlist of the three deliberately public pages. (3) The provider seam — lib/video/provider.ts is 151 lines, five methods, and no Bunny type crosses it; its own header says switching providers is a new implementation plus one line in lib/video/index.ts. That is already the abstraction a rebuild would claim to introduce. (4) The module seam — modules/registry.ts is one import and one map entry per module (9 today), and modules/contract.ts carries `shape` and `content` fields that exist precisely so no surface outside modules/ ever switches on a module type; tests/unit/registry.test.ts enforces it. A billboard is five small files (Editor.tsx, Guest.tsx, index.ts, resolve.ts, schema.ts, 10.8 KB total). This is the theme-store architecture already built. (5) Rendering — middleware.ts is 122 lines of pure rewrite logic delegating to tested pure functions in lib/tenant.ts, serving path-mode tenancy and custom domains onto the same guest tree. The one structural change the refactor makes is to move guest locale off a cookie and onto the header middleware already sets (middleware.ts:16-19 sets three), and to stop awaiting searchParams in the page shell, so app/c/[slug]/page.tsx:21 `export const revalidate = 3600` becomes true instead of aspirational. That is the whole architectural delta: the shape is right, the enforcement and the caching are not.
benefits: Every slice ships. R2 (the liveOnly fix) is one day and removes both high-severity findings; the photo half is already written in the working tree. A rewrite ships nothing for 8-12 months and the first thing it ships is a regression risk to 6 live orgs.

The two findings that actually matter to a guest are data-layer bugs, and the fix (a driver conformance suite executed against both drivers in CI, ~8 days) makes the whole class impossible rather than fixing one instance. A Go rewrite writes a new hand-rolled driver with no conformance suite and reintroduces the class.

Generated Supabase types (`supabase gen types typescript`, ~2 days) give compile-time checking of the ~20 column maps against the live schema — the precise type-safety benefit the Go/Java case rests on, obtainable inside TypeScript for two days instead of nine months.

The frontend is untouched. 15,921 lines of React 19 / Tailwind v4 / CSS-custom-property theming, 9 modules, 7 built-in themes plus platform-authored ones, and the customizer's live preview of the real guest components all keep working. CLAUDE.md's one deliberate deviation — the guest tree is client-renderable so the customizer mounts real guest components — is satisfied by having one implementation, and a port cannot improve on one.

The 1.5-second-on-4G Phase-0 definition of done survives. Guest pages are server-rendered today and the refactor makes them genuinely ISR-cached; a Go backend plus a React SPA would have to rebuild server rendering for the guest tree or give the budget up.

Retains 659 unit/component tests (9,312 lines) and 212 E2E tests (2,807 lines) — 37.4% line coverage, 79.9% branch coverage as measured — rather than re-deriving them. Re-deriving an equivalent suite is itself a multi-month project nobody prices.

Retains 24 applied migrations and the production data behind them. A port must either keep this schema exactly (in which case Postgres was never the problem) or migrate live weddings, which is the one operation that cannot be rolled back.

Retains the operational knowledge that was paid for in incidents — the Bunny webhook pointing at a stale alias (docs/GO-LIVE.md:213-244), the TUS resumable-offset handling CLAUDE.md flags as where the schedule slips, the signed-directory playback tokens. These are provider quirks, not TypeScript quirks, and a rewrite rediscovers each one.
Runtime dependency surface is 14 packages. The 'unmanageable' feeling is not npm sprawl and a rewrite does not reduce a number that is already small.

Cost of being wrong is one sprint. If after the refactor `pnpm verify` is honestly green, staging exists, and shipping a feature still takes a month, the diagnosis was wrong and the port case is then strictly stronger for having 26 fewer confirmed defects in the spec it would be built from.
costs_and_losses: 3.5 engineer-months (~60 working days plus 25% slack) of a one-person-plus-agent team, spent on debt rather than on Razorpay, WhatsApp delivery, the theme store or direct-to-client onboarding. That is a real opportunity cost and the honest headline number.
Roughly 4 calendar months at realistic allocation, because feature work and 10 weddings/month of support continue alongside. Sequenced so that R2, R3 and R5 land inside the first six weeks.
The codebase gets bigger, not smaller. Expect +3,000-4,000 lines of test and conformance code. Anyone whose complaint is literally 'too many files' will be less happy, not more.

About ₹4,300/month of new recurring infrastructure: Vercel Pro (~₹1,900) so all six cron jobs are platform-scheduled instead of four of them hanging off a GitHub Actions workflow that disables itself after 60 days of repo inactivity, and Supabase Pro (~₹2,400) for branching so staging exists. Total steady state at current volume ≈ ₹11,800/month against a Bunny bill of ₹7,534 (cost.json, 10 weddings/month).

Nine of the fourteen documentation findings that matter require deleting or archiving documents someone wrote — USAGE-GUIDE.md as a 521-line stale duplicate, GO-LIVE.md as three stacked completed runbooks, ARCHITECTURE.md as predating a third of the shipped surface. Deleting your own writing is slow work with no visible output.

The conformance suite needs a real Supabase branch in CI, which means CI stops being hermetic (today .github/workflows/ci.yml pins DATA_DRIVER=memory and VIDEO_DRIVER=fake for every job). That is a new flake surface and a new secret in CI.

Splitting CreateWizard (1,006 lines, 26 useState calls in the component) into a reducer plus step components is a rewrite of the most business-critical screen with no user-visible change. It is the single riskiest item in the plan and it is optional.
It does not feel like a fresh start. There is no morale dividend, and 'we fixed the lint config' is not a story anyone enjoys telling.
risks: Refactor drift: a debt sprint with no end date becomes a permanent state. Mitigation — the ten items below are the whole list, each with a day estimate, tracked in docs/NEXT.md as a numbered block, and the sprint ends when they are done even if new findings arrive.

The org-scoping test (R6) is the one item that can fail on day one if written from the reviewer's assumption rather than the code: the verify pass showed the proposed guard list would reject 11 legitimate admin pages because page-level guards use different function names, and app/admin/login, /register and /new are deliberately unauthenticated. Write it from a read of the tree, not from the finding.

Making the guest page genuinely static (R3) changes when a published edit becomes visible. lib/catalogue-cache.ts and app/api/cron/reconcile/route.ts:84-86 both already note that revalidatePath does nothing because the route reads cookies; once it is truly cached, every publish path must revalidate correctly or an operator hits Publish and sees nothing change. This needs an E2E test before it ships, not after.

The conformance suite could pass and still miss a difference, because a recording stand-in pins query shape rather than Postgres behaviour — exactly the caveat the new tests/unit/supabase-query-shape.test.ts writes into its own header. Only the CI-against-a-real-branch half closes that, and it is the half most likely to be dropped under time pressure.

Bus factor stays at one. 179 commits from one author plus an agent between 8 Aug and 13 Sept; if that person stops, the refactor does not help. Neither does a port — it makes the same risk worse for 8-12 months — but neither option addresses it and it should be named.

Vercel platform ceilings remain. SCALE-PLAN §3 puts the function-invocation ceiling at roughly 300 weddings/month, and the Hobby two-cron limit is why four jobs live in GitHub Actions today. Pro raises both; it does not remove the class of constraint, and a genuinely large scale event forces a hosting conversation the refactor has only deferred.

TypeScript's structural typing is what let a driver implementation drop an options parameter and typecheck. The fix here is a conformance test and an object-parameter convention, not the compiler. A Go implementation would have failed to compile. This is the one place the rival case is correct on the merits, and buying a compile-time guarantee costs 8 days here versus 9 months there.
what_it_does_not_fix: Commerce does not exist and refactoring does not build it. There is no Razorpay code, no webhook, no invoice table, no Razorpay environment variable anywhere; the `plans` table has zero rows and no reader; catalogue-level entitlements are dead code; every rupee so far moved by bank transfer with a platform admin typing a free-text audit reason afterwards. What is sold (100-200 GB per plan, docs/PRICING.md:27-31) is not what is enforced. Four unsynchronised documents carry live-looking prices and no price exists in code, so nothing can test the ladder. That is greenfield work in any language.

Infrastructure cost is unchanged, because the cost is Bunny and Bunny is a correct decision. cost.json models self-hosting at 7.3x Bunny's cost at 10 weddings/month and 2.4-2.8x at 60, including people; infra alone only crosses at roughly 900-1,000 weddings/month on the R2 stack. Neither refactoring nor porting moves that line.

It does not make TypeScript a stricter language, and it does not give a code-generated query layer the way sqlc does in Go. Generated Supabase types plus Zod at the edges get most of the way; 'most of the way' is an honest description, not a complete one.

It does not remove the single-author bus factor, and it does not make the product manageable by someone who has not read it. 26,000 non-test lines with 15% comment density is a two-week read for a new engineer — short, but not zero.

It does not fix the Bunny webhook's un-verifiable configuration. That URL is a dashboard setting no code in the repo can read, verify or change, `pnpm preflight` cannot check it, and it has already caused one real incident. The only proof it is correct after a domain change remains uploading a real film and watching it reach ready.

It does not build captions, playback speed, WhatsApp or SMS delivery, the studio-facing lapse dashboard, or the deletion job that would actually reclaim Bunny storage — all named as absent across the subsystem maps, all features rather than debt.

It does not decide the open questions that are Sandeep's to decide: whether unlisted catalogues' photographs should be signed, whether a passcode should grant downloads, and what the price ladder actually is. Nothing technical unblocks those.
triggers_to_revisit: Sustained volume above ~300 weddings/month, where SCALE-PLAN §3 puts the Vercel function-invocation ceiling. Even then the correct move is a Go or Rust service for the two hot paths (the progress heartbeat and the playback-token mint) behind the interfaces that already exist, not a whole-app port.

CPU-bound work genuinely entering the product — in-house transcoding, on-device-quality photo processing, ML on faces. That is a separate service in whatever language suits it, called through lib/video/provider.ts's existing five-method seam. It is not a reason to retype lib/catalogue-access.ts.

A second and third engineer join who are Java or Go native and demonstrably cannot be productive in this codebase after a two-week onboarding. Today the population is one author plus an agent, and both are productive in it.

The refactor completes, `pnpm verify` is honestly green, staging exists, and shipping a normal feature still takes more than a week. That falsifies the diagnosis in this document and the port case becomes the strongest one on the table.

Vercel or Supabase pricing or platform terms change such that the hosting line exceeds the 17%-of-revenue model at 60 weddings. The answer then is the Dockerfile that already exists plus the four crons it would need, not a language change.
A second confirmed production data-correctness bug of the liveOnly class appears after the conformance suite is in CI. That would mean the seam itself, not its instrumentation, is the problem.
migration_path: R2 (1 day, week 1) — Finish the liveOnly fix. lib/db/supabase-repository.ts:1624-1643 already carries the photo half plus a new tests/unit/supabase-query-shape.test.ts in the working tree, uncommitted. Add the titles half: listTitles at :1390-1391 filters publishedOnly on `.eq('published', true).eq('status','ready')` with no live_at predicate, against lib/schema.ts:461-462's own doc comment ('Null means the couple cannot see it, whatever published says'), and decide deliberately what app/api/playback/token/route.ts:35-41 should gate on so the operator's own preview stays possible. Commit and ship. This closes both high-severity findings.

R6a (1 day, week 1) — Replace `next lint` with `eslint .` in package.json:14. Reproduced: `npx next lint` reports clean while `npx eslint middleware.ts modules themes` reports 4 no-restricted-properties errors, because .eslintrc.json never exempted those paths — `next lint`'s default directory set did. Extend tests/unit/registry.test.ts's walk (currently app/, components/, lib/ only) to modules/, themes/ and middleware.ts. `pnpm verify` stops being greener than the codebase. Next 16 removes `next lint` anyway, so this is owed regardless.

R5 (10 days, weeks 2-3) — The ops floor. Move to Vercel Pro and put all six jobs in vercel.json, ending the dependency on a GitHub Actions workflow whose own header (.github/workflows/notify-drain.yml:14-15) states it disables itself after 60 days of repo inactivity and which today drives lifecycle, warnings, notify and the hourly synthetic check — i.e. every alert path. Add explicit maxDuration to the two long crons (grep finds none anywhere) and a resumable cursor to app/api/cron/usage/route.ts:51-65, whose nested serial provider loop currently dies by wall clock and leaves no job_runs row at all. Stand up a staging Vercel project and a Supabase branch (N-87 already prices this as a day plus two free accounts). Add a migrations ledger table and wire the existing scripts/migrate.ts as the applier, replacing docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:113-116's paste-into-the-SQL-console instruction and its admission that 'there is no ledger'. Fix .claude/skills/ship/SKILL.md:46 to curl mehfilbox.com rather than a Vercel alias the backlog itself calls luck.

R1 + R6b (10 days, weeks 4-5) — Driver parity, permanently. A conformance suite of behavioural assertions run against both MemoryRepository and a real Supabase branch in CI, covering at minimum every method taking a filter option. Add `supabase gen types typescript` and type the ~20 field-to-column maps against the generated Database type (only 2 are held to their schema today, and the most-edited entity's map is a private inline object with no test). Add the org-scoping test, written from a read of the 34 admin route files and 11 admin pages and their five real guard names, with app/admin/login, /register and /new on an allowlist.

R3 (6 days, weeks 6-7) — Make the guest page actually cached. app/c/[slug]/page.tsx:21 declares revalidate = 3600 while the route is dynamic three times over: lib/guest-locale.ts:22-23 calls cookies() unconditionally, app/c/[slug]/page.tsx:64-70 awaits searchParams, and the passcode read at lib/catalogue-access.ts:57 is conditional. Move locale onto the header middleware.ts:16-19 already sets, push searchParams handling into a client boundary, and fold the per-card dynamic reads into the cached bundle. Ship behind an E2E test that proves a Publish is visible immediately, because lib/catalogue-cache.ts:13-17 and app/api/cron/reconcile/route.ts:84-86 both record that revalidatePath currently does nothing here.

R4 (4 days, week 8) — The heartbeat. components/streaming/useProgressHeartbeat.ts:5 fires every 10 seconds and app/api/progress/route.ts costs five Supabase round trips per beat, which against SCALE-PLAN's 300-guests-by-20-minutes assumption is roughly 12x the whole system's modelled 30,000 invocations/month. Move to 30 seconds plus visibilitychange/pagehide flushes, collapse the five reads into one RPC, and read the play_events retention column that already exists and nothing reads.

R8 (5 days, week 9) — Bound the queries. Add limits and pagination (PostgREST's default row cap truncates without error today), fix the platform console's per-org round trip, chunk the unbounded `.in()` that returns HTTP 414 on a large studio, and give catalogueCounts and the platform console the bounded reads the Repository interface's own comment set out to provide.

R10 (6 days, weeks 10-11) — The three tracked security gaps. Sign photo URLs (N-83: lib/photos/bunny.ts:34 never signs, against lib/video/bunny.ts:96-148's signed equivalent) and extend scripts/preflight.ts's photo check to verify token enforcement the way :241-251 does for video. Add rate limiting to the three guest endpoints that skip it while every sibling calls lib/http/rate-limit.ts. Add a Content-Security-Policy. Requires Sandeep's decision on unlisted catalogues first.

R7 (10 days, weeks 12-14, optional) — UI confidence. Component tests for the four largest untested components, then split CreateWizard (1,006 lines, 26 useState) into a reducer plus per-step components and fix the draft loss on reload at steps 1-2. Do this last: it is the highest-risk, lowest-user-visible item, and if the sprint has to be cut, cut here.

R9 (5 days, ongoing) — Collapse the documentation to the three files CLAUDE.md already names: PRODUCT, PROGRESS, NEXT. Archive USAGE-GUIDE.md, GO-LIVE.md and ARCHITECTURE.md; fix README's 'Known gaps'; correct CLAUDE.md's enforced-rules table so it describes what R6 now actually enforces; put one price table in code so the ladder is testable. Nine of the fourteen documentation findings matter inside twelve months, and stale maps are the largest single contributor to the codebase feeling unmanageable.
evidence: The stack is already React 19 and Tailwind v4 with CSS custom-property theming: package.json dependencies list react 19.0.0, react-dom 19.0.0, next 15.5.23 and tailwindcss ^4.0.0; app/globals.css:1 is `@import 'tailwindcss'` with 104 CSS custom properties from :13; themes/contract.ts:5-11 states a theme is 'a validated token set, nothing more' and themeTokensSchema at :23-40 is the whole theme surface. 'Port to React and Tailwind' describes the current repository.

Scale of what a port must rebuild, from §1 of the nine subsystem maps: guest streaming with one route tree mirrored onto custom domains; studio console with a five-step wizard and per-catalogue screens; couple accounts with handover/claim; platform console with ten health probes, audit trail and theme authoring; two swappable AuthProvider drivers plus a structurally separate platform_admins identity; commerce with entitlements, credits and a four-state lifecycle ladder; a notification queue with eight bilingual templates behind a provider seam; media-infra with TUS resumable upload, a signed Bunny webhook, six crons and the Repository seam; and the themes/customizer layer with seven built-in themes, house styles, the module registry and a live preview that mounts the real guest components. Measured: 40 pages, 60 API routes, 70 components, 9 modules, 24 migrations, 103 Repository methods (lib/db/repository.ts), 42 Zod schemas in lib/schema.ts, 41 files carrying `server-only`, 83 files carrying 'use client'.

Line split that decides what a port actually replaces: app 8,270 + lib 10,940 + middleware 122 = 19,332 server-side lines to re-express in Go or Java; components 13,326 + modules 2,213 + themes 382 = 15,921 lines that are React and Tailwind in every option, i.e. 55% of source is out of scope of a backend port by construction.

All 49 verified findings carry real=true across verify-scalability.json (12), verify-maintainability.json (11), verify-deployability.json (12) and verify-documentation.json (14); 26 carry matters_next_12_months=true; exactly 2 are high severity and both are the same liveOnly root cause (verify-maintainability finding 1 and verify-scalability finding 3).

The high-severity finding, verified: lib/db/repository.ts:343 declares `listPhotosForCatalogue(catalogueId, options?: { liveOnly?: boolean })`; lib/db/memory-repository.ts:924 filters on liveAt; lib/catalogue-cache.ts:65 passes { liveOnly: true }; the Supabase implementation ignored it. The titles half is still live at lib/db/supabase-repository.ts:1390-1391, which filters publishedOnly on `.eq('published', true).eq('status','ready')` and never on live_at.

The fix-speed evidence for 'not unmanageable': as of 16 Sept the working tree carries `M lib/db/supabase-repository.ts` and an untracked tests/unit/supabase-query-shape.test.ts, both uncommitted. lib/db/supabase-repository.ts:1632-1641 now applies `.not('live_at', 'is', null)` under a comment naming the 15 September review, and the new test pins the query shape through a recording Supabase stand-in. One person plus an agent, inside a day, on the finding two independent reviewers called the worst in the codebase.

Attribution of the 49 findings to language or framework, done finding by finding: one (the driver dropping an options parameter and still typechecking) is partly TypeScript's structural typing; two are Next.js specifics — lib/guest-locale.ts:22-23 calling cookies() unconditionally plus app/c/[slug]/page.tsx:64-70 awaiting searchParams defeating `export const revalidate = 3600` at :21, and `next lint`'s default directory set hiding 4 real eslint errors in middleware.ts (:23:22, :34:8, :74:5, :74:46) that .eslintrc.json:27 never exempted. The remaining 46 — the 10-second heartbeat at components/streaming/useProgressHeartbeat.ts:5 with five Supabase round trips per beat in app/api/progress/route.ts:38-73, four of six crons on a GitHub Actions workflow that disables itself after 60 days (.github/workflows/notify-drain.yml:14-15, vercel.json:9-18 registering only two), no maxDuration anywhere, no migration ledger (docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:116), no staging (docs/NEXT.md:181-194, .github/workflows/ci.yml:12-18 pinning DATA_DRIVER=memory), unsigned photo URLs (lib/photos/bunny.ts:34), unbounded reads, and fourteen documentation findings — are language- and framework-neutral and reappear in a Go rebuild unless someone chooses otherwise, which they can equally choose here.

The seams a rebuild would claim to introduce already exist and are small: lib/catalogue-access.ts is 88 lines and its header states it is the one place a guest request is authorised, with the ordering (lapsed before published at :37-48, premiere before passcode at :51-54, draft is never a 404) legible in a single screen; lib/video/provider.ts is 151 lines and five methods whose header says switching to Cloudflare is one new implementation plus one line in lib/video/index.ts; middleware.ts is 122 lines delegating to pure functions in lib/tenant.ts; modules/registry.ts wires 9 modules as one import and one map entry each, with modules/contract.ts:25-41 carrying `content` and `shape` fields whose stated purpose is to stop any surface outside modules/ from switching on module type. A billboard module is five files totalling 10.8 KB.

Test asset that survives a refactor and does not survive a port: 66 unit/component files, 9,312 lines, 659 tests; 17 E2E files, 2,807 lines, 212 tests (56 skipped by design). Measured coverage 37.4% of lines, 62.6% of functions, 79.9% of branches (coverage/coverage-summary.json). The weakness is concentrated in UI, which is the half a backend port does not replace anyway.

Dependency surface: 14 runtime dependencies (@dnd-kit x4, @supabase/ssr, @supabase/supabase-js, hls.js, lucide-react, next, react, react-dom, server-only, tus-js-client, zod). Whatever 'unmanageable' means here, it is not dependency sprawl.

Delivery velocity in this stack: 179 commits between 2026-08-08 and 2026-09-13 from one author plus an agent, producing 9 subsystems, 40 pages, 60 API routes and 24 migrations. Pricing a 19,332-line server-side port with a re-derived 871-test suite at that same velocity gives 9-14 engineer-months before parity, with zero customer-visible value delivered in the interval.

Infrastructure, from cost.json: at 10 weddings/month Bunny is ₹7,534/month against ₹19,971 self-hosted infra-only and ₹54,971 including people (7.3x); at 60 weddings/month ₹45,207 against ₹54,508 / ₹1,24,508 (2.4-2.8x); no breakeven inside the modelled range once people are counted, and infra alone crosses only at roughly 900-1,000 weddings/month on the R2 stack. Refactoring leaves this line alone, which is the correct treatment of it.

What refactoring cannot reach, from map-commerce.md §7: no payment code, no webhook, no invoice table and no Razorpay environment variable anywhere in the repository; `plans` is a real table with zero rows and no reader; catalogue-level entitlements are dead code in practice; docs/PRICING.md:27-31 sells storage the code does not enforce; renewal is entirely manual; four unsynchronised documents carry live-looking prices while no price exists in code.
